doc.title: Greg Caputo interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

title: First lessons with Joe Morello in New Jersey
summary: He faces intimidating players in Morello's studio, is put in his place, and learns pedal and pad work.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: So you moved on from that instructor. It was pretty apparent to you at this time that I’m going to make a living as a drummer.

Yes. I moved on to Joe Morello at that time. And the impact was — although there had been a void of time because he had practice and everything, he was on the road quite a bit. And I went down to see him in Irvington, New Jersey. And I got frightened in a big way because there were some big names around me. He has like, if you will a “green” room, and he picks and chooses who he’s going to take next. If you call up and ask Joe Morello for a lesson time, it’s twelve o’clock for everybody. So at that time anyway, and we were all in this pool, and I was listening to some of these drummers warm up and it frightened me. There were some fantastic players there. And I was like half the speed of everyone. And—

Right. Joe Sepchik had brought me down. Joe Sepchik was one of Joe Morello’s students. And he came into the lesson with me, and he was Joe Morello’s teacher and there was some small talk then I started to play. And Joe frightened me. He let me know exactly where I was on the totem pole, and I went for it. I went after it. I took the challenge and I worked very hard and really became a technique freak for a while, and wanted to get up to that level, and I did, but also Joe is a phenomenal teacher and he told me, “Time and space too, kid.”
Well I’m curious, that first time with him, and he said to you well play something. What do you play in a situation like that? Do you solo, do you play some time, or is it a combination of both?

Well he had me play a little bit on the pad, and I played some rudiments for him, okay, yes I see, okay well let’s try your reading. Well I had studied with a reading teacher and I read the things down cold. He says okay fine, your reading’s fine, let’s go over to the drumset. And I sat behind the drumset. Well let’s hear your foot. And I can remember he had a certain pedal tension the way that he played, and I couldn’t play anything and he went yuck. We need to work on that. So from now on I brought my own pedal to his lessons. He’s a master teacher too. But like I say the only warning I would give anybody that would listen to this tape, be ready. Because he’s not, he’s a master, and it could frustrate you.
